body.x: Two-N (CEO Jaehun Kim) announced its participation in CES 2025 from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. The company will exhibit in the K-Startup Pavilion, highlighting its cutting-edge water treatment and desalination solutions centered around its proprietary Membrane Distillation (MD) technology.

Established in 2021, Two-N aims to address the high energy consumption and system complexity of traditional water treatment technologies, such as Reverse Osmosis (RO). The company’s innovative MD technology provides an eco-friendly and economical alternative, setting a new benchmark for the water treatment industry.

The MD technology operates under low-pressure and low-temperature conditions, making it compatible with renewable energy sources like solar and waste heat, significantly reducing energy usage. Two-N’s custom-developed superhydrophobic membrane prevents contamination and damage, ensuring easy maintenance and long-term stability. This reduces costs and energy consumption, enabling its application in desalination, wastewater treatment, oil-water separation, and clean water production.

Two-N has developed foundational technologies to scale its MD solution for plant-level applications and has been working towards commercialization. In South Korea, the company supplies equipment for purifying wastewater generated during secondary battery manufacturing, demonstrating its MD technology’s high efficiency and environmental benefits in industrial settings. It is also actively participating in the “Deep Tech TIPS” national research project for seawater desalination.

Internationally, Two-N has exported oil-water separation systems to Japan’s Mitsubishi Chemical Corporation (MCC) and is collaborating with major Japanese companies on pilot projects. Recently, the company signed a partnership with Singaporean industrial firm Cyclect to strengthen its global presence.

body.x: At CES 2025, Two-N will showcase its water treatment technologies, emphasizing the advantages of its MD-based desalination solution. The company highlighted its MD technology’s exceptional energy efficiency, environmental friendliness, and reliability, positioning it as a practical solution for seawater desalination and broader water scarcity challenges.

MD technology achieves over 80% water recovery rates, outperforming conventional desalination methods and enabling efficient water utilization in regions with severe water shortages. Operating at low pressure and temperatures (55–80°C) reduces energy consumption by approximately 30% compared to RO systems. Further savings are possible when integrated with renewable energy sources.

The superhydrophobic membrane design minimizes contamination and membrane damage, offering an extended lifespan and lower maintenance costs. MD technology is versatile, with applications ranging from seawater desalination to industrial wastewater treatment, oil-water separation, and concentrated brine recovery. Its operation minimizes the use of chemical agents, reducing environmental impact and supporting businesses' ESG goals.

A Two-N representative expressed the company’s interest in partnering with U.S. water treatment firms capable of managing construction and operation, which is essential for scaling MD technology to plant-level applications. While Two-N has successfully developed the core technology for MD scale-up, it faces challenges such as building global brand recognition and overcoming initial market entry barriers. Integration with existing systems and securing testbeds to demonstrate the technology’s superiority remain critical hurdles.

“Collaborating with partners who can test our technology in real-world operations and co-develop commercialization pathways would amplify our opportunities for market entry and exports,” the representative added. Two-N is committed to further research and promotional activities to enhance its global presence, with its participation in CES 2025 being a pivotal step.
